context: Standardize Clay Pit's analytical and machine learning workloads on Snowflake for scalability and ecosystem alignment.
implications: ELT pipelines and BI tooling will target Snowflake as the definitive warehouse
Data contracts and governance must accommodate Snowflake schemas and role hierarchy
Future analytics enhancements should evaluate Snowflake-native capabilities first

context: Initial proposal was to build a hypothesis testing system that simulates owner questions across 10-15 different customer personas (clones) to evaluate business decisions like menu changes, pricing, or service offerings.
rejection_reason: User clarified they only have one detailed customer persona (Aniket Sharma from NVIDIA), not multiple customer clones. The multi-persona simulation approach was misaligned with the actual use case.
what_was_proposed: Owner asks question → LLM extracts hypotheses → Simulate across 10-15 customer personas
Each persona represented different demographics, preferences, price sensitivity
Concurrent simulations to gather diverse feedback
Aggregate sentiment analysis across persona types
Generate insights based on persona-specific responses
why_rejected: Only working with single persona (Aniket), not multiple customer types

decision: Rejected: Single-persona multi-scenario hypothesis testing CLI
context: Second proposal adapted to single persona (Aniket) but generated multiple scenario variants to test hypotheses across different contexts (time of day, budget levels, event types, communication channels).
rejection_reason: User clarified the actual need was a straightforward customer service chatbot, not a hypothesis testing/simulation system. The scenario-matrix approach was over-engineered for the requirement.
what_was_proposed: Owner asks question → LLM extracts hypotheses → Generate scenario matrix
Scenario dimensions: time_of_day × budget × event_type × channel
Simulate Aniket's response in each scenario variant (e.g., 'Monday 9am + $1200 budget + team lunch')
Generate insights about which contexts work best for a given hypothesis
Complex flow with hypothesis detection, scenario generation, concurrent simulations
why_rejected: User wanted a normal multi-turn customer service chat, not a hypothesis testing system

context: Final design is a straightforward multi-turn chatbot where the agent speaks TO Aniket (or user playing as Aniket), using his detailed persona to anticipate preferences and adapt communication style.
rationale: Simpler design that matches actual use case: a customer service agent that knows the customer's profile and provides personalized service.
implementation: Single Agent with rich system prompt containing Aniket's full persona
Time-aware behavior (auto-detects or override with --time flag)
Multi-turn conversation loop (similar to existing chat-ordering-cli.ts)
No hypothesis extraction, no scenario generation, no simulations
Just a smart agent that knows customer preferences and adapts accordingly
key_features: Loads aniket_profile.json with detailed persona data
Adapts tone based on time of day (structured AM, efficient midday, collaborative PM, urgent evening)
Knows favorite dishes, dietary requirements, budget ranges
Uses tech analogies, provides Slack-ready bullet summaries
Remembers NVIDIA milestones and sustainability values

context: Building toward FastAPI backend integration requires full observability of CLI operations, user interactions, and agent behaviors.
rationale: FastAPI backend will need to replay sessions, analyze conversations, and trigger workflows based on logged events. JSON Lines format (logs.jsonl) is FastAPI-compatible and enables streaming log analysis.
implementation: SystemLogger class logs every operation to sessions/{sessionId}/logs.jsonl
Log categories cover entire system: session lifecycle, user I/O, agent calls, data ops, order flow, payments
Structured JSON format with timestamps, categories, data payloads for easy backend parsing
Console output formatted for CLI UX, file output optimized for API consumption
Auto-flush mechanism ensures logs persist even if process crashes
implications: All new functionality must integrate with SystemLogger
FastAPI can tail logs.jsonl for real-time monitoring
Analytics can aggregate logs across sessions for insights
Debugging simplified with comprehensive operation traces
Performance metrics captured automatically with trackOperation()

context: Need to support multi-session conversations where users can pause and resume ordering flows across CLI invocations.
rationale: Single-run conversations don't reflect real customer behavior. Users may need to check with team, get budget approval, or add items across multiple sessions. Session persistence enables this while maintaining context.
implementation: SessionManager creates unique session IDs (sess_{timestamp}_{random})
Each session stored in sessions/{sessionId}/ directory with session.json + logs.jsonl
Session state includes: conversation history, order state, context variables, profile updates
CLI prompts user to resume active sessions or start new one
Sessions closed with status: completed, abandoned
Automatic session listing shows last 3 active sessions with turn counts
implications: FastAPI backend can serve session state via REST API
Users can have multiple concurrent sessions (different projects/events)
Session history enables better recommendations and context awareness
Must implement session cleanup/archival strategy for old sessions
Session resume shows last 6 conversation turns for context

context: aniket_profile.json should grow with each interaction, capturing new delivery addresses, preferences, team information, and behavioral patterns.
rationale: Static profiles become stale. Real customer relationships involve learning over time. Each conversation reveals new information that should be permanently captured to improve future interactions.
implementation: ProfileUpdater uses GPT-4.1 to extract new learnings from conversation history
Extraction looks for: delivery addresses, contacts, event types, preferences, budget patterns
Updates categorized by confidence (high/medium/low) and action (append/replace/merge)
User reviews and approves updates before applying to aniket_profile.json
Profile backups created before each update with timestamp
Learning extraction runs automatically on session exit
implications: aniket_profile.json becomes a living document, not static config
Profile updates must be reviewed to prevent AI hallucinations
Backend can trigger learning extraction after each session
Need governance around profile schema evolution
Backup files accumulate over time - need cleanup policy
future_enhancements: Scheduled profile review UI for admins

decision: Reduced agent verbosity via instruction engineering
context: Initial agent responses were too verbose and contained unnecessary explanations. Customer (Aniket) values efficiency and conciseness.
rationale: Over-explanation wastes time and doesn't match customer communication style. Bullet points and direct answers align better with 'polite but decisive' and 'medium-high context but wants concise recaps' profile traits.
implementation: Updated system prompt with COMMUNICATION RULES section emphasizing conciseness
1-3 sentence responses unless details requested
Bullet points for options, not prose
Skip pleasantries after greeting
Bad/good example pairs in prompt to guide behavior
Reduced temperature from 0.8 to 0.7 for more focused responses
Explicit instruction: Target Verbosity LOW despite profile saying medium-high
implications: Faster interactions, less token usage
Better alignment with customer persona
May need A/B testing to find optimal verbosity level
Different personas may need different verbosity settings
Example-driven prompting significantly improves response quality

decision: Order state machine with CLI-level confirmation flow
context: Need structured order flow: detect intent → draft → confirm → checkout → complete
rationale: Agent can't reliably handle multi-turn confirmation workflows. CLI-level state machine ensures proper flow control and logging.
implementation: OrderState enum: chatting | confirming | processing | completed
detectOrderIntent() scans user input for ordering keywords
extractOrderDraft() parses agent response for items, quantities, totals
detectConfirmationIntent() recognizes yes/no patterns
State persisted in session for resume capability
Stripe checkout triggered only after explicit confirmation
implications: Clear separation: agent suggests, CLI controls workflow
State transitions fully logged for debugging
Easy to add validation steps (inventory check, pricing, etc.)
FastAPI can implement same state machine server-side
Prevents accidental order placement from ambiguous agent responses

context: CLI is prototype; production system will have FastAPI backend serving web/mobile clients.
rationale: CLI architecture should anticipate backend needs to minimize refactoring. Structured logging, session management, and profile learning are backend-ready patterns.
scaffolding_decisions: JSON Lines logging format (FastAPI can stream/parse easily)
Session state stored as JSON files (can move to database later)
Clear separation: data layer (CSV, profiles), business logic (agents, orders), presentation (CLI)
All async operations to match FastAPI async patterns
Utilities designed as importable modules, not CLI-specific code
future_backend_endpoints: POST /sessions/{id}/messages → send user message, get agent response
GET /sessions → list active sessions for customer
POST /sessions/{id}/learnings → extract and apply profile updates
migration_path: 1. Extract business logic into shared library (rc/core/)
2. Wrap SessionManager/SystemLogger in FastAPI service layer
5. Build REST API endpoints matching scaffolded patterns
6. CLI becomes thin client calling API instead of direct logic
7. Add WebSocket support for real-time agent streaming
8. Build web/mobile UIs consuming same API

decision: CSV-based order history with dynamic loading
context: Order history currently hardcoded in CLI; need to load from orders.csv and order_details.csv at project root.
rationale: Centralized data source enables consistency across tools. CSV format is simple, human-readable, and easy to update.
implementation: loadOrderHistory() reads orders.csv and order_details.csv
Joins on order_number field to combine customer + order data
Returns OrderHistory[] sorted by order number descending
Injected into agent system prompt for context-aware suggestions
Custom CSV parser handles quoted fields and special characters
implications: Agent can reference past orders naturally in conversation
Bulk discount suggestions based on historical patterns
Easy to add new historical data without code changes
Future: migrate to database but keep same data structure
Order history loaded once per session for performance

decision: Stripe checkout placeholder with visual feedback
context: Need payment integration mockup for demo/testing before real Stripe implementation.
rationale: Placeholder allows testing full order flow without payment processor setup. Visual elements (QR code, checkout URL) make demo more realistic.
implementation: createCheckoutSession() generates mock session with realistic structure
Simulates 1.5s processing delay for realism
Displays formatted checkout UI with order ID, amount, session ID, timestamp
ASCII art QR code placeholder
Checkout URL follows Stripe pattern: https://checkout.stripe.com/pay/{sessionId}
All checkout events logged for backend integration planning
future_production_implementation: Replace mock with real Stripe API calls
Add webhook handlers for payment confirmation
Implement idempotency keys for retry safety

decision: Order editing not supported in current implementation
context: Users cannot modify an order draft after it's been created. If they want to change items, quantities, or details, they must cancel and start over.
why_this_limitation: Order state machine only supports forward flow: chatting → confirming → processing → completed
Agent responses would need to be parsed and merged with existing draft (complex)
Session state doesn't track 'previous draft' for comparison
current_workaround: User must decline the order when prompted 'yes/no to confirm'
User can make a new request with corrections
Session preserves conversation history for context
future_implementation: Implement draft merge logic in order-state.ts
Add commands: 'edit order', 'remove item X', 'change quantity of Y to Z'
Create OrderDraftEditor class to handle modifications
Track draft versions for undo/redo capability
Add validation before each state transition
impact: Medium - Users can work around by declining and restarting, but UX is not ideal for complex orders with many items
priority: High for production - essential for good UX
